canonical_question: How does the 'loss of Mn' observed in the FLiBe salt study impact the mechanical properties of the alloy in service?

question_variants.question: How does the 'loss of Mn' observed in the FLiBe salt study impact the mechanical properties of the alloy in service?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that the loss of Mn in FeNiCrCoCu (cited work by Wang et al. or similar context in FLiBe salt study) prevented the dissolution of Cr. However, it does not explicitly state the impact of this Mn loss on the *mechanical properties* of the alloy in service. It only mentions the effect on Cr dissolution in the molten fluoride salt.

answers.answer: The text mentions that loss of Mn prevented the dissolution of Cr in molten fluoride salt, but does not link this specifically to the impact on mechanical properties.
answers.measurement_outcome: Loss of Mn prevented dissolution of Cr
answers.boundary_limitation: No data provided on the resulting impact of this compositional change on mechanical properties in service.
evidence_spans: This paper investigated the effects of different crystal orientations, temperatures, and strain rates on the mechanical properties and plastic deformation mechanisms of an equiatomic FeNiCrMn HEA using molecular dynamics simulations.
The results revealed that the FeNiCrMn HEA exhibited significant anisotropy under loading along different orientations, with the maximum yield stress observed along the <11-1> direction.
During the elastic stage, all crystals maintained a single FCC structure.
